content:
Formula: Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT)
Exact Expression: X_k = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x_n \cdot e^{-i \frac{2\pi}{N} k n} \quad k = 0, \dots, N-1
Definitions: Linear transformation converting a finite sequence of equally-spaced samples of a function into an equivalent-length sequence of complex frequency coefficients.
Derivation/Reference: Carl Friedrich Gauss (Fast Fourier algorithm manuscript, 1805); J. W. Cooley & John W. Tukey (1965)
Example: Input impulse delta[n] = [1, 0, 0, 0] -> X_k = [1, 1, 1, 1] (flat constant spectrum across all harmonics)
Domain: mathematical_physics
Assumptions: Uniform sampling interval Ts satisfying Nyquist-Shannon criterion fs >= 2 B
Common Errors: Confusing continuous Fourier Transform with discrete DFT; failing to account for spectral leakage and circular convolution
